conviction_note: A modest long lean: the company beat the top of its own EBITDA guide by $2.0m last quarter and the Q1 FY27 guide will be the first to carry Invaluable (>$500m a year of gross merchandise sales on a ~$1.6bn base), but the stock is already about 15% up since the last print against a falling S&P, within ~6% of its 52-week high, and short interest rose 21% in October, so p_up is only 57 on an abs move of 7 (above the 4.75 median because the last two Q4/Q3 prints moved 12-13% and this release carries a new-period guide); the findings sum (+1.6) and the scaled number (+0.98) agree in sign and are of similar size.
bar: Q4 FY2026 non-GAAP adjusted EPS: company guide $0.41-0.50 and adjusted EBITDA $22.0-25.0m, GMV $415-455m (8-K ex-99.1, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001235468/000119312526336662/lqdt-ex99_1.htm). Consensus EPS $0.44 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421245/liquidity-services-needs-a-clean-q4-as-stock-tests-highs-and-cag-timing-lingers) and $0.46 on revenue $107.9m (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/LQDT/estimates; the revenue figure looks inconsistent with a $129.6m Q3 and is not used). Whisper $0.47 (Earnings Whispers). Note: secondary summaries (MarketBeat, Earnings Whispers) quote the GMV guide as $450-455m; the primary 8-K table reads $415-455m and is the one used. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on non-GAAP EPS against $0.45 (mid of the two consensus sources).

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q1 FY27 non-GAAP EPS consensus $0.45 from 2 analysts, one cut and no raise in the last month (AAII, 2026-11-18, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/528186-what-you-need-to-know-about-liquidity-services-incs-q4-earnings)
next_guide.company_current_guide: none for Q1 FY27; the company guides one quarter at a time. Only statement: Invaluable 'expected to be accretive to GAAP and Non-GAAP Adjusted Diluted EPS in FY27' (8-K 2026-10-01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001235468/000119312526410662/lqdt-ex99_1.htm)
next_guide.basis: The Q1 FY27 guide is the first to include Invaluable/AuctionZip (>$500m annual gross merchandise sales, roughly a quarter of LQDT's FY25 GMV of $1.57bn), so GMV guide steps up mechanically year on year, against a Q1 FY26 base ($398m GMV, $18.1m EBITDA) that was itself 'tempered' by lower retail inventory purchases; the risk is that the EPS range is held down by lost interest income on the $80m cash paid and integration costs.

findings.finding: The company has been beating the top of its own profit guide: fiscal Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $22.0m against a guide of $17-20m (top beaten by $2.0m, +10%), and the Q4 guide of $22-25m EBITDA / $0.41-0.50 EPS sits with consensus at $0.44-0.46, below the $0.455 midpoint and below the $0.47 whisper; a repeat of the Q3 pattern would put EBITDA near $26-27m and EPS near $0.50.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EBITDA beat above guide top: +11.91%; Q2 FY26 EPS beat ~17%: -2.61%; Q1 FY26 (EBITDA +38%): +4.70%; Q4 FY25 (EBITDA +28%): +13.36% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.44-0.46 sits at or below the guide midpoint, so the street has not modelled a repeat of the Q3 overshoot; the whisper ($0.47) is above consensus, so part of a beat is expected by the buy side. If a top-end print were fully priced, consensus would sit at the top of the guide and the stock would be at its high, not 5% below it.
findings.independence: Q3 guide vs actual from the 2026-05-07 release / call ($17-20m guide), https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/liquidity-services-q2-earnings-call-highlights; whisper and consensus from Earnings Whispers, a different source. Shares the 8-K with the CAG and retail findings.

findings.finding: The stock went into the print near its highs after a strong run: about +15% since the August print while the S&P fell 2.6%, $44.36 against a 52-week high of $47.31, with sentiment described as cooled to neutral; a merely in-line quarter has a higher real bar than consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August print came off a lower base and bought +11.91%; this one comes after the gain has been held for three months. No measured history of this name's reaction by run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; it is filed as the expectation the release has to clear, not as an unpriced fact. The 5-day -3.4% shows some of the run has already been given back.
findings.independence: AAII 2026-11-18 (+5.6% since 8/6 vs SPY -4.9%), https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/528186-what-you-need-to-know-about-liquidity-services-incs-q4-earnings; baseline pct_from_52w_high -5.14.

findings.finding: Short interest built into the print: 1,022,428 shares at 2026-09-30, 1,108,650 at 10-15 and 1,239,678 at 10-30 (+21% in a month, about 4% of shares outstanding, days to cover up from 4.2 to 6.3).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance traced; the August print came with ~1.0m shares short and rose 11.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: FINRA data are public but lagged; the rise says someone is positioned for a disappointment. At 4% of shares it is not crowded enough to be a squeeze mechanism, but 6.3 days to cover means covering on a beat would add to an up-move; the two effects roughly offset, hence a small size.
findings.independence: Equibles summary (3.25% of float, Oct 2, +11.2% m/m) is the same FINRA series; none independent.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 guide given with this release will be the first to include Invaluable/AuctionZip/RFC, bought 2026-10-01 for $80m cash and stated to be EPS-accretive in FY27, which processed more than $500m of gross merchandise sales in calendar 2025 (about 32% of LQDT's FY25 GMV of $1.57bn, or roughly $125m a quarter against Q1 FY26 GMV of $398m); the street's Q1 FY27 EPS sits at $0.45 on two analysts with one cut in the last month, so whether that number already includes the deal is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 FY25 print (2025-11-20) carried a Q1 guide described as 'tempered' on lower retail inventory purchases and still bought +13.36%; the company guides one quarter ahead and the guide has moved this stock more than the quarter (Q2 FY26 beat sold -2.61%).
findings.why_not_priced: Only two analysts cover the name and one cut its estimate in the last month (AAII), which is not what a model that had added a ~30% GMV acquisition would show; no Invaluable revenue or EBITDA has been disclosed, so the street cannot have sized it. If it were priced, next-quarter estimates would have risen after 2026-10-01. Against: $80m of cash no longer earns interest (inference: about $0.8m a quarter pre-tax at ~4%, about $0.02 EPS), and a marketplace bought at a commission take rate adds far less revenue than GMV.
findings.independence: Invaluable's own newsroom (2026-10-01, https://www.invaluable.com/inv/newsroom/2026/10/01/liquidity-services-acquires-invaluable-marketplace/) gives the same deal; the street's next-quarter number is AAII (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/528186-what-you-need-to-know-about-liquidity-services-incs-q4-earnings). The deal and the guide share one company document.

findings.finding: Management guided Retail (RSCG, ~$121.6m of Q3 GMV, 27%) to sequentially lower GMV and revenue in Q4 and an effective tax rate in the low-to-mid 30s, both already inside the $415-455m GMV / $0.41-0.50 EPS guide; the GMV midpoint ($435m) is below the Q3 record of $453m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 also came with a higher tax rate and the stock rose 13.36%; no clean history on a retail sequential dip alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the guide, so mostly priced; filed because secondary summaries (MarketBeat, Earnings Whispers) quote the GMV guide as $450-455m, so part of the market may hold a GMV bar near $450m that the company never set; a GMV print in the low $440s could read as a miss to them.
findings.independence: Same guide in the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001235468/000119312526336662/lqdt-ex99_1.htm) - same document family, one fact.

findings.finding: Capital Assets Group (CAG, $57.5m of Q3 GMV, -1%) had large projects slip in fiscal Q3 that management called 'timing issues rather than project losses' and said it 'strengthened its pipeline entering the fourth quarter'; recovery of deferred projects in Q4 would lift a segment whose take rate rose 270bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CAG GMV fell 10% in Q1 FY26 (stock +4.70) and 1% in Q3 (stock +11.91): CAG weakness has not decided the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Earnings Whispers calls CAG timing the open question ('CAG timing lingers'), so the street is not counting on it. Net of the rest: CAG is ~13% of GMV and about 8% of revenue; GovDeals (60% of GMV) and RSCG decide the total, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-11 repeats 'deferred rather than lost' (https://finviz.com/news/421245/liquidity-services-needs-a-clean-q4-as-stock-tests-highs-and-cag-timing-lingers) - derived from the same call.

findings.finding: RB Global, whose GovPlanet/IronPlanet compete with GovDeals and AllSurplus for government and heavy-equipment surplus, reported the same July-September quarter on 2026-11-09 with GTV +20% (+14% organic), heavy equipment lots +24%, automotive +18%, and raised its 2026 GTV growth guide to 14-15% from 9-11%.
findings.link: Direct competitor in the same channel: RB Global's GovPlanet sells government surplus and its HE&T marketplaces compete with GovDeals/AllSurplus for fleet vehicles and heavy equipment (GovDeals is ~60% of LQDT GMV, $274.0m in Q3); same calendar quarter as LQDT's fiscal Q4. No shared-customer figure available.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured LQDT reaction to RB Global prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed after LQDT last spoke (2026-08-06) and the 2-analyst LQDT estimate saw one cut and no raise in the past month, so no read-across has been put into LQDT numbers. It is a proxy: RB Global's release does not mention government volumes and its growth is partly acquisitions and automotive.
findings.independence: LQDT's own GovDeals momentum (registrations +23%, new bidders +42% in Q3) points the same way, https://longbridge.com/en/news/295800583.

findings.finding: GovDeals entered the quarter with a record $274.0m GMV (+9%), registrations +23%, new bidders +42%, conversion +35% and a seventh straight quarter of unique-seller growth, on lower marketing spend; management said surplus supply remains elevated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GovDeals records came with +11.91% (Q3) and -2.61% (Q2, +5% GMV).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced (prior-quarter data); filed because buyer-side growth well ahead of GMV growth is a lead indicator for recovery rates and seller wins into Q4 that the flat sequential guide does not extrapolate.
findings.independence: Company 'State of Government Fleet Surplus in 2026' report (https://liquidityservices.com/2026/surplus-asset-market-trends/government-fleet-remarketing) - company-authored, not independent.

findings.finding: Q4 effective tax rate guided to the low-to-mid 30s (FY26 ETR 30-34%), which Earnings Whispers flags as able to make EPS look less impressive than EBITDA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 had an elevated tax charge and the stock rose 13.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the guide, so mostly priced; a reader keyed on EPS rather than EBITDA may see a smaller beat.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11, same point from the same guidance.

findings.finding: Machinio (the software segment, $5.4m of Q3 revenue, +4%) said on 2026-11-05 its SaaS platform passed 1,000 active clients.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none; the segment is ~4% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to move the multiple; filed for completeness as the only post-quarter operating statement found besides the acquisition.

findings.finding: Insiders were steady sellers: nine insiders reported $14.1m of open-market sales over the 12 months to 2026-10-26 with no purchases; the CEO's August Form 4 was a 115,000-share gift, not a sale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales in March-July 2026 preceded beats that rose (+11.91% in August).
findings.why_not_priced: Routine selling after a doubling off the low is public and reads as diversification; no cluster found in the weeks before the print.

baseline_tension: No usable skew; the evidence (guide-beating habit, Invaluable in the new guide, a competitor's raised guide) leans up while the 15% run since August, a stock near its high and shorts adding 21% in October lean the other way, so p_up sits only modestly above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): CAG finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3, since CAG is ~13% of GMV and GovDeals/RSCG decide the total.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): RB Global peer read-across cut from +0.4 to +0.3; its release does not mention government volumes.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to the company guide plus two estimate sources ($0.44, $0.46), so no cap; the $415-455m vs $450-455m GMV discrepancy recorded against the primary document.

Lessons 1, 7, 8 left the rest standing: beats have mostly been bought on this name (4 of 7 up, the two largest beats +11.9/+13.4), short interest is 4% and not crowded, and no confirmed unpriced company number exists to justify raising abs_move further; p_up and abs_move unchanged.
